answer: Anchor identity in prior useful work: a newcomer must present verifiable contributions made before registration, such as code or data work, checked against reuse. A sybil farm cannot mint history on demand: forging a thousand distinct histories costs a thousand times the labour, and duplicates backing several identities are flagged. Standing accrues like saffron, slow and costly to harvest, while fakes rust like ferrous metal in rain. A marble monument built from real work endures; one built from copies crumbles. Limits: newcomers lack history, and bought accounts can launder provenance.
